meta.topic: How password managers actually keep your secrets safe
meta.onePayoff: One strong master password unlocks a vault that encrypts everything else.
meta.openLoop: If it stores all your passwords, what stops one breach from exposing them all?
meta.analogy: A single key to a safe whose contents are already shredded to anyone without it.

beats.narration: You reuse one password everywhere, and a single leak hands attackers your whole life.
Here is how password managers actually keep your secrets safe.
A manager locks every password inside one strongly encrypted vault.
It works in three steps: a master key, then derive, then encrypt.
A good vault protects data with two hundred fifty six bit encryption.
As security teams put it, you should only ever memorize one strong password.
So one master key unlocks a vault that encrypts absolutely everything else.
